title: Exact finite-step support locality for the all-bond Q3 split approximant
question: For a finite Q3 graph, does an onsite-plus-all-bond split step map every cylinder support into its closed one-layer neighborhood, so that N split steps depend only on the rooted N-ball and not on the distant shape?

model.bch: The second commutator vanishes because the first commutator is a configuration multiplier.
model.onsite_layer: Each exact onsite factor is site-local and preserves cylinder support, conditional on the declared site flow.
model.support_map: S -> S union {y: y is adjacent to some x in S}
model.split_step: Either order of the onsite layer and the all-bond kick has support contained in the closed one-layer neighborhood.
model.N_step: The support after N steps is contained in the closed N-ball of the initial support.

statement.finite_shape_locality: If two rooted finite graphs have isomorphic induced N-balls around the source, the N-step split support trajectories agree under that isomorphism.
statement.qft_role: This supplies an exact finite-N exhaustion-locality input; it does not supply a uniform Trotter rate or the N-to-infinity common dynamics.

adversarial_review.check: Every bond generator is a polynomial in commuting q coordinates; no momentum commutation is used in the factorization.
The sign is derived from [p_x,V]=-i*hbar*c*sum_{y~x}q_y and checked for both time signs; the second commutator is explicitly zero.
Support preservation of the onsite factor is a declared site-local flow hypothesis, not inferred from finite matrices.
The N-ball statement is exact only at fixed split-step count N; it does not interchange N-to-infinity with volume exhaustion.
Only rooted induced N-ball agreement is used; no global graph isomorphism or arbitrary-shape uniform norm is claimed.
The support calculation is an algebraic cylinder statement and does not prove unbounded-domain invariance or a common core.
Uniform Trotter convergence, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
R337 checks exact finite graph neighborhoods and scalar BCH bookkeeping only; it does not formalize the unbounded Q3 flow.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks exact rational BCH and finite neighborhood fixtures; Python checks all declared graph/source/order/sign trajectories.

qft_interface.closed: At fixed split count N, support is confined to the N-ball and is determined by the rooted N-ball, for both term orders and time signs.
qft_interface.open: A volume- and cutoff-uniform analytic Trotter rate, unbounded common core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, N-to-infinity exhaustion interchange, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the exact finite-N locality lemma as the combinatorial input for a uniform split-to-exact Trotter estimate on the Q3 common core; if that estimate cannot be made uniform in N and volume, record the obstruction before common-alpha promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite-step support theorem. It is not a thermodynamic dynamics theorem or a QFT/Clay result.
no_overclaim: The package proves only algebraic finite-N support locality under a declared site-local onsite-flow hypothesis. It does not prove the N-to-infinity Trotter limit, exhaustion independence, common alpha, KMS/GNS, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A, TECT production or a Clay result.
